holidays.name: National Chocolate Ice Cream Day
holidays.description: A day to grab a scoop, a cone, or a whole tub of the rich, cocoa-packed flavor that has been rivaling vanilla for generations. Dish, cone, milkshake or sundae: every format counts.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance held every June 7. Its creator is unclear, but it has become a fixture on the summer dessert calendar.
holidays.funFact: Chocolate ice cream has roots in ancient Mexico, where chocolate was first enjoyed, and it gained popularity in France centuries later.

holidays.name: National VCR Day
holidays.description: A nostalgic salute to the video cassette recorder, the clunky box that let people record TV shows, rent movies and rewind (politely, of course) in their living rooms. Celebrate by dusting off an old tape and enduring some tracking lines.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It pays tribute to the VCR, which ruled home entertainment from the late 1970s through the 1990s.
holidays.funFact: The VCR changed how people watched TV by letting them record shows and watch them whenever they wanted. It also launched the video rental store era.

holidays.name: June Bug Day
holidays.description: A buzzing tribute to the shiny, clumsy beetles that bonk into porch lights on warm early-summer nights. It's a lighthearted reminder to notice the little critters that arrive with the season.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is held every June 7 to celebrate these nocturnal insects and summer biodiversity.
holidays.funFact: June bugs are named for the month when they typically emerge, and they are famous for flying into lights at night.
